text.p: Rick Fehr
shot a second consecutive round of 65 to take the second-round
lead at the Walt Disney World Classic at 14 under par Friday.
Fehr's 65 came at the host Magnolia course, giving him the
lead by a stroke over three players -- Payne Stewart, who shot
a 63 at Disney's Lake Buena Vista (LBV) course, Jim Carter,
whose 65 was at the same course and first round co-leader
Frank Lickliter, who had a 68 at Magnolia.
Two strokes off the lead at 12 under par was a group of
eight players, including Tiger Woods, who shot a 63 at LBV.
The pro-am tournament rotates between three of Disney's
resort courses -- the LBV, the Palm, and the Magnolia, where
the final round will be played on Sunday.
Fehr, who has said after 11 seasons on the Tour he is
reducing the time he spends away from his family, played no
practice rounds and spent the early part of the week with his
children at the Disney theme parks.
Fehr had seven birdies and no bogeys on Friday, starting
with a birdie at the first hole in the somewhat dim light of
sunrise.
"I think we had to play number one by Braille," Fehr said.
Woods, as always drawing the largest crowds on the course,
had five birdies and an eagle in his first eight holes.
His only bogey of the day came at Lake Buena Vista's par
three seventh hole, which was playing to a microscopic 105
yards. Woods sent a sand wedge shot over the green then missed
an eight foot par putt.
"I flagged it, but I had too much speed at the bottom of
the swing. It was downwind, too," Woods said.
As the last full field event of the 1996 PGA Tour, this
tournament is the last chance for several top players to earn
enough money to get into the top 30 and qualify for next
week's Tour Championship and all of next year's majors. It
also is the last chance for many of the lesser players to
reach the top 125 to keep their PGA cards.
Woods, 34th on the money list, probably needs to finish
12th or better to make it into next week's field at Southern
Hills C.C., while Stewart can do no less than win. Lickliter
needs at least a top 10 to make it into the top 125.
For Fehr, in 92nd place on the money list, the top 30 is
out of reach but his exemption is safe.
